title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for diabetes and foot pain.

HPI: The patient is a 64-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes. He reports stable glucose levels but continues to experience numbness and tingling in both feet. He has been diagnosed with polyneuropathy. The patient states that the symptoms are persistent but have not changed in severity over the last three months. He denies any recent falls or acute injuries to the lower extremities.

Medication List: Insulin, metformin, and a daily multivitamin.

Exam: The patient is alert and in no acute distress. Physical exam reveals intact sensation in the upper extremities. Lower extremities show diminished sensation to light touch and vibration in the toes. Muscle strength is 5/5 in all lower extremity groups. Skin is intact without breakdown or ulcerations.

Assessment: 1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stable on current regimen. 2. Polyneuropathy, which the provider notes is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan: Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin. Monitor blood glucose levels daily. Schedule a follow-up appointment in three months to evaluate sensation and medication efficacy.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
